column11: Yoma 75a: ‘§ With regard to donations for the Tabernacle, the verse states: “And they brought yet to him free-will offerings every morning” (Exodus 36:3). This teaches that pearls and precious stones fell for the Israelites with the manna. It states: “And the rulers [nesi’im] brought the onyx [shoham] stones” (Exodus 35:27). A tanna taught that the word nesi’im means actual clouds brought them. As it states: “As clouds [nesi’im] and wind without rain so is he that boasts himself of a false gift” (Proverbs 25:14). column11: Yoma 73b:13-88a:12: ‘Rava said that Rav Yehuda said: The volume of a large date that they said is larger than an egg-bulk. The Sages have an accepted tradition that with this amount of food, the mind of the one who eats is settled, and he is not afflicted. Less than this amount, the mind is not settled. column13: But consummate perfection occurs through complete repentance out of love, where deliberate sins are transformed into merits, granting eternal life (Yoma 86b); achieved when the heart burns with fire for Hashem until all dross is consumed, becoming holy unto Hashem, revealing that "all our works You have wrought for us," past sins functioning retroactively as a transgression for the sake of Heaven, which is greater than a mitzvah performed for ulterior motives (Nazir 23b).

column15: Yet one not yet fully refined must repeatedly acknowledge his lack of wholeness, compelled to plead at every hour that Hashem complete his deficiency. For this reason an intoxicated person is forbidden to pray, because he feels no lack, all the world appearing flat and unhindered before him (Yoma 75a); and if he prays he speaks falsehood before Hashem, for prayer exists only when acknowledging one's deficiency.

column13: The explanation of this is as stated (Psalms 33:6): "By the word of Hashem were the heavens made," for the Blessed Name did not fashion the cosmos like a craftsman fashioning an object, but through His speech alone; meaning that His divine utterance "Let there be such an entity" constitutes the very energy, vitality, and preservation of that object, as it is said (Nehemiah 9:6): "and You preserve them all," and as it is said (Psalms 119:89): "Forever, Hashem, Your word stands firm in heaven," the utterance through which the heavens were made standing permanently embedded within them to vivify and sustain them.

column15: And because through the constricting power of this Name creation was brought forth, it followed that creation remained strictly within its bounds, unable to expand into transgression.
